verbaseln.et: Borrowed from Low German verbaseln (chiefly reflexively “to lose one’s way”, but also as in Standard German), an iterative-diminutive of verbasen (“to baffle, confound”), from Middle Low German vorbāsen. Cognate with Dutch verbazen, Norwegian forbause, etc.

s: to distort, to corrupt (to change a word or phrase through folk etymology or general ignorance of the original form, especially when borrowing from a foreign language)
Im Liede werden als Mörder des Königs bezeichnet: Rockenzan, Girsich. Derart verballhornte der deutsche Dichter die fremdsprachlichen Namen.
In the song, the following are named as the king's killers: Rockenzan, Girsich. That is how the German lyricist distorted the foreign names.
to mock, to jokingly refer to [with als] (to purposefully distort a word in such a way to make fun of what is being referred to)
Kennen Sie dieses Liedchen, das die Nazis verballhornt? Es enthält eine tiefe Wahrheit über die fehlende Courage von Machtmenschen.
You know that little tune mocking the nazis? It contains a deep truth about the lakcking courage of people striving for power.

那么，从社会学考察的角度看，什么是「政治」团体？

过去，各种各样的团体，从氏族开始，都把物理暴力当作完全正常的手段。

今天我们只把它理解为：一个政治团体的领导，或者对这种领导施加影响；在今天，也就是一个国家的领导。
